sentences.text: A vast, featureless expanse stretched to the horizon in every direction, offering the eye nothing to rest on.
Undulating, golden dunes rippled like a frozen sea, each crest as sharp as a blade.
The searing, merciless sun beat down on their heads from a sky scoured of every cloud.
A shimmering heat haze wavered above the plain, turning distant rocks to liquid.
They trudged through the sand for hours, their water bottles lighter with every mile.
A hot, grit-laden wind scoured their faces and filled their mouths with dust.
Fine, shifting sand hissed down the slope and filled each footprint as soon as it was made.
Two vultures wheeled overhead with the patience of creatures that know how the story ends.
A scorpion scuttled under a rock, and small, darting lizards flickered across the stones.
A snake slithered across the sand, leaving its signature in a long, looping scrawl.
The parched, cracked earth baked in the midday glare, split into plates like a broken dish.
The sheer, ochre canyon walls glowed red at sunset, as though lit from within by embers.
Within minutes the blinding, choking sandstorm obliterated the track and blotted out the sun.
At last a line of palms rose out of the haze, marking the cool, green oasis.
He staggered on without water, his lips split, his tongue a strip of leather.
The sand cooled swiftly after dark, and they huddled round the embers through the frigid, silent night.
The lake dissolved as they drew near; it had been nothing but a mirage, a cruel trick of the light.
Palm fronds rustled in the evening breeze beside the dark, still water of the well.
The camels plodded in single file along the crest of the dune, their shadows stretching far down the slope.
The constellations blazed overhead in a vast, star-strewn sky, brighter than she had ever known them.
Gaunt, towering cacti stood like sentries along the dry, stony riverbed.
Bleached, scattered bones lay beside the track, half claimed by the sand.
Nothing lived in the barren, sun-baked wasteland but a few withered thorn bushes.
Soft, rose-pink dawn light crept over the dunes, and for one brief hour the desert was gentle.
The wind shrieked across the dunes, tearing at the tents and flaying every inch of exposed skin.
For three days they saw no living thing, not even a bird in that immense, indifferent sky.
The market at the oasis seethed with traders, bleating goats and the grumbling of tethered camels.
In the cool of evening the dunes softened to shades of amber and violet, and a deep quiet settled.
By noon the rocks were too hot to touch, and even the lizards had retreated into shade.
Dust devils eddied across the plain, spinning themselves out and rising again.
